units.text: This circular informs the industry that the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) will extend the parallel run period of its new online application/submission system for investment products, e-IP, by one month to 29 November 2024. After the extended period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by the Investment Products Division (IPD)1 must be submitted to IPD via e-IP from 30 November 2024.
Background

Following the “Circular on launch of e-IP application/submission system on WINGS” dated 8 July 2024, the SFC launched e-IP on its WINGS2 portal on 29 July 2024 to streamline and enhance the efficiency of processing new product applications and post-authorisation/registration submissions to IPD.

A three-month period of parallel run from the launch of e-IP up to 29 October 2024 was provided at the initial stage. During this period, the SFC continues to accept applications and submissions via existing channels.
Parallel run period extension and upcoming enhancements
Since its implementation, the SFC has closely monitored the functioning of e-IP and actively engaged with industry participants to obtain their feedback on user experience.

While e-IP has garnered widespread industry support and is running smoothly, new features and more advanced settings will be introduced to further enhance user experience based on users’ comments. To facilitate these enhancements, the SFC will extend the parallel run period of e-IP by one month to 29 November 2024.
Full adoption of e-IP

Starting 30 November 2024, ie, after the parallel run period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by IPD must be submitted via e-IP. The current submission requests from IPD via the IP E-submission system will be integrated into e-IP, including reporting of net asset values, large redemptions and suspensions of dealing. In addition, e-IP users can also settle recurring annual fees associated with relevant investment products through the new system.
Feedback and enquiries
The SFC will continue to review and enhance the operation of e-IP where practicable. If you have any questions, please contact the relevant case officers.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission
End

1 Investment-linked assurance schemes, mandatory provident fund products, open-ended fund companies, paper gold schemes, pooled retirement funds, real estate investment trusts, unit trusts and mutual funds and unlisted structured investment products.
2 Web-based INteGrated Service.

assumptions.statement: “After the extended period” is read as beginning immediately after 29 November 2024.
The word “must” applies to applications and submissions, while the listed integrated requests clarify examples rather than limit the duty.

candidate.controlled_language: The compulsory e-IP duty clearly begins on 30 November 2024, but the complete set of covered submission types and any post-transition exceptions are unresolved.
candidate.revision_reason: Alternative reading: the duty is compulsory for the specified IPD submission requests, including the examples integrated from the IP E-submission system, but the text leaves open whether other communications or exceptional filings may continue through another channel with IPD approval. This reading treats the integration sentence as potentially delimiting the operational set rather than merely illustrating it.

Extending the parallel run carries forward the existing-channel acceptance described for that run.

candidate.controlled_language: Selected control—compulsory e-IP submission route: if a person makes an application or submission to IPD concerning an investment product administered by IPD on or after 30 November 2024, that filing must be submitted via e-IP. Existing channels remain accepted during the extended parallel run through 29 November 2024. The control specifies the route for covered filings; it does not independently create filing obligations, reporting frequencies or a compulsory e-IP route for annual-fee payments. Within the formal scope, a true result means this route condition is met and a false result means it is unmet; outside scope, no route-compliance conclusion is drawn.
candidate.revision_reason: This reading applies the transition to each covered filing made from the stated date, including filings concerning existing products or cases where they qualify as submissions. It preserves the separate permission to pay annual fees through e-IP. A competing rule limited to cases initiated after the transition, or conditioned on completed enhancements, lacks sufficient textual support. The strongest uncertainty is the boundary of covered submissions and the treatment of pending-case events under the unavailable referenced materials.

candidate.controlled_language: Selected control: compulsory e-IP submission route from 30 November 2024. Each in-scope application or submission made on or after that date must use e-IP. Existing-channel acceptance continues during the extended parallel period through 29 November. Neither planned enhancements nor the practicability qualification creates a stated exception. The result tests only route satisfaction within scope; it does not determine whether a filing is required, timely or substantively adequate.
candidate.revision_reason: The strongest supported reading uses the date of each submission event. For example, an in-scope supplementary submission made on 2 December for an application initially lodged on 28 November falls within the route requirement. A case-opening-date approach would exempt it, but this packet provides no affirmative support for that grandfathering rule, so it is an unresolved question rather than a second proposed reading. An ordinary existing-channel submission on 29 November remains within parallel running; the same event on 30 November engages the compulsory route. Optional annual-fee settlement does not independently engage this control.

candidate.controlled_language: For the selected compulsory e-IP submission-route control, existing channels remain accepted during the parallel run extended through 29 November 2024. From 30 November 2024, covered filings must use e-IP. Practicability qualifies SFC improvements only, and annual-fee settlement remains an optional facility. The Boolean formalization tests the route only within its stated scope; out-of-scope filings are not classified as failures.
candidate.revision_reason: The existing-channel permission is a temporary allowance carried forward by the extension. The hypothesis that 'where practicable' excuses users from mandatory e-IP filing fails because that qualifier attaches to the SFC's review and enhancement activity. An enhancement-completion condition likewise lacks textual support. Attaching 'During this period' exclusively to the original October endpoint ignores the express extension of that same parallel run. No materially supported rival exception is retained; the strongest uncertainty is treatment of filings spanning the transition.

units.text: This circular informs the industry that the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) will extend the parallel run period of its new online application/submission system for investment products, e-IP, by one month to 29 November 2024. After the extended period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by the Investment Products Division (IPD)1 must be submitted to IPD via e-IP from 30 November 2024.
Background

Following the “Circular on launch of e-IP application/submission system on WINGS” dated 8 July 2024, the SFC launched e-IP on its WINGS2 portal on 29 July 2024 to streamline and enhance the efficiency of processing new product applications and post-authorisation/registration submissions to IPD.

A three-month period of parallel run from the launch of e-IP up to 29 October 2024 was provided at the initial stage. During this period, the SFC continues to accept applications and submissions via existing channels.
Parallel run period extension and upcoming enhancements
Since its implementation, the SFC has closely monitored the functioning of e-IP and actively engaged with industry participants to obtain their feedback on user experience.

While e-IP has garnered widespread industry support and is running smoothly, new features and more advanced settings will be introduced to further enhance user experience based on users’ comments. To facilitate these enhancements, the SFC will extend the parallel run period of e-IP by one month to 29 November 2024.
Full adoption of e-IP

Starting 30 November 2024, ie, after the parallel run period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by IPD must be submitted via e-IP. The current submission requests from IPD via the IP E-submission system will be integrated into e-IP, including reporting of net asset values, large redemptions and suspensions of dealing. In addition, e-IP users can also settle recurring annual fees associated with relevant investment products through the new system.
Feedback and enquiries
The SFC will continue to review and enhance the operation of e-IP where practicable. If you have any questions, please contact the relevant case officers.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission

Parallel run period extension and upcoming enhancements
Since its implementation, the SFC has closely monitored the functioning of e-IP and actively engaged with industry participants to obtain their feedback on user experience.

While e-IP has garnered widespread industry support and is running smoothly, new features and more advanced settings will be introduced to further enhance user experience based on users’ comments. To facilitate these enhancements, the SFC will extend the parallel run period of e-IP by one month to 29 November 2024.
The SFC will continue to review and enhance the operation of e-IP where practicable. If you have any questions, please contact the relevant case officers.
